newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYBEANS MIXED, AUGUST UP ON EXPORT TALK.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYBEANS MIXED, AUGUST UP ON EXPORT TALK.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were mixed early Wednesday, with August posting sharp gains on talk of demand for soybeans in export markets.
"They're still talking about beans being wanted at the U.S. Gulf," said one floor trader.
Traders said there was talk China had bought U.S. soybeans, but U.S. exporters could not offer confirmation of a sale early Wednesday.
In other export news, Taiwan bought 112,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for shipment during October or first half-November, depending on origin.
New crop soybeans labored under pressure from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's forecast for a record 1997/98 (Sept/Aug) soybean crop of 2.744 billion bushels, traders said.
Crop weather this week has generally been considered good for soybeans. Periodic rain showers continue to pepper dry areas of the Midwest and alleviate some moisture stress.
At 1055 CDT, November soybeans were down three cents at $6.08-1/2 per bushel and other months were up 9-1/4 to down 4-1/2.
